\chapter{Bigger, Best, and How Long}
\label{ch:ml-bigger-best-and-how-long}
\hlchaptermodality{346}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can compare two things with -ekkāḷ, name the best with ēṟṟavuṁ, and say how long something has gone on or lasted.}

Complete ML-R346-comparing-and-time: than with -ekkāḷ, most with ēṟṟavuṁ, for N years now with -āyi, since with mutal, and the new letter \ml{ഋ}.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{അതിനെക്കാൾ} (atinekkāḷ)}{അതിനെക്കാൾ (atinekkāḷ)}]{\ml{അതിനെക്കാൾ} (atinekkāḷ) — than that}

\label{lesson:ML-C346-atinekkal}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}big\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}more\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}a good one\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{valiya}, \emph{kūṭutal}, \emph{nallatŭ}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: X-\ml{നെക്കാൾ}, \textquotedblleft{}than X\textquotedblright{}}]
Malayalam has no \textquotedblleft{}bigger\textquotedblright{}. It says \textquotedblleft{}than that, this is big\textquotedblright{}. Put the thing you compare against in the object form, \textbf{\ml{അവനെ}}, \textbf{\ml{അതിനെ}}, \textbf{\ml{എന്നെ}}, and add \textbf{-\ml{ക്കാൾ}}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{അതിനെക്കാൾ} \ml{വലുതാണ്}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{itŭ atinekkāḷ valutāṇŭ.} — \textquotedblleft{}This is bigger than that.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ട്രെയിൻ} \ml{ബസിനെക്കാൾ} \ml{വേഗത്തിൽ} \ml{പോകും}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭreyin basinekkāḷ vēgattil pōkuṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}The train goes faster than the bus.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ചായയെക്കാൾ} \ml{കാപ്പിയാണ്} \ml{ഇഷ്ടം}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{enikkŭ cāyayekkāḷ kāppiyāṇŭ iṣṭaṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}I like coffee more than tea.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ml{വലുത്}} is \textquotedblleft{}a big one\textquotedblright{}, made from \textbf{\ml{വലിയ}} the way \textbf{\ml{നല്ലത്}} is made from \textbf{\ml{നല്ല}}. You will also meet the ending with a long vowel, \textbf{-\ml{ഏക്കാൾ}}, as in \textbf{\ml{അതിനേക്കാൾ}} (\emph{atinēkkāḷ}); both are correct, and they mean the same.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: \ml{ഏറ്റവും}, \textquotedblleft{}the most\textquotedblright{}}]
Put \textbf{\ml{ഏറ്റവും}} before the quality, and it is the top of the scale:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{ഗ്രാമത്തിലെ} \ml{ഏറ്റവും} \ml{വലിയ} \ml{വീടാണ്}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{itŭ grāmattile ēṟṟavuṁ valiya vīṭāṇŭ.} — \textquotedblleft{}This is the biggest house in the village.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{-\ml{ലെ}} is \textquotedblleft{}in, of\textquotedblright{} before a noun. \textbf{\ml{ഏറ്റവും} \ml{നല്ലത്}} is \textquotedblleft{}the best one\textquotedblright{}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}This is bigger than that.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The train goes faster than the bus.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I like coffee more than tea\textquotedblright{}, then the other way round
  \item \textquotedblleft{}This is the biggest house in the village\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}this is the best one\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}Than him\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{avanekkāḷ.}}) \textquotedblleft{}Than me\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{ennekkāḷ.}}) \textquotedblleft{}The biggest\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{ēṟṟavuṁ valiya.}})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഋതു} (ṛtu)}{ഋതു (ṛtu)}]{\ml{ഋതു} (ṛtu) — a season}

\label{lesson:ML-C346-rtu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say \textquotedblleft{}the rainy season\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}summer\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{maḻakkālaṁ}, \emph{vēnalkkālaṁ}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}the most\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{ēṟṟavuṁ}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഋതു}}
\textbf{\ml{ഋതു}} — \emph{ṛtu} — \textquotedblleft{}a season\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{മഴക്കാലം} \ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ഏറ്റവും} \ml{ഇഷ്ടമുള്ള} \ml{ഋതുവാണ്}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maḻakkālaṁ enikkŭ ēṟṟavuṁ iṣṭamuḷḷa ṛtuvāṇŭ.} — \textquotedblleft{}The rainy season is my favourite season.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{പഴയ} \ml{കണക്കിൽ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{വർഷത്തിൽ} \ml{ആറ്} \ml{ഋതുക്കൾ} \ml{ഉണ്ട്}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paḻaya kaṇakkil oru varṣattil āṟŭ ṛtukkaḷ uṇṭŭ.} — \textquotedblleft{}In the old reckoning, a year has six seasons.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

In everyday talk, \textbf{-\ml{കാലം}} names each season, as in \textbf{\ml{മഴക്കാലം}}. \textbf{\ml{ഋതു}} is the word for the season itself, in writing, songs and the calendar. Most speakers say it close to \emph{rutu}.

Its first letter is new; the next lesson puts it in your hand.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഋതു}} (\emph{ṛtu}) $\leftarrow$ Sanskrit \emph{ṛtu}, \textquotedblleft{}a fixed time; a season\textquotedblright{}, taken over whole (Monier-Williams). The same dictionary records the later Sanskrit count of six seasons in a year, the count the old reckoning keeps.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{ṛtu}, then the plural \emph{ṛtukkaḷ}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The rainy season is my favourite season.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}In the old reckoning, a year has six seasons.\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \textbf{\ml{ഋതു}} mean? (\textbf{a season.}) Which ending names each season in everyday talk? (\textbf{-\ml{കാലം}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഋ} (ṛ)}{ഋ (ṛ)}]{\ml{ഋ} (ṛ) — the letter that opens \ml{ഋതു}}

\label{lesson:ML-W346-vocalic-r}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \textbf{\ml{ൃ}} and \textbf{\ml{ര}} once each, and name them. (The \emph{ṛ} sign, as in \textbf{\ml{കൃഷി}}; and \emph{ra}.)

Now say \textbf{\ml{ഋതു}} (\emph{ṛtu}), \textquotedblleft{}a season\textquotedblright{}. This lesson takes its first letter out and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ml{ഋ}}
\textbf{\ml{ഋ}} — \emph{ṛ}, the Sanskrit vowel \emph{r}, at the start of a word. Malayalam says it \emph{ru}, with a short \emph{u} after the \emph{r}: \textbf{\ml{ഋതു}} sounds close to \emph{rutu}.

After a consonant it is the sign \textbf{\ml{ൃ}}, as in \textbf{\ml{കൃഷി}} and \textbf{\ml{സുഹൃത്ത്}}. At the start of a word it stands as a letter of its own, \textbf{\ml{ഋ}}. Only a few learned words begin with it.

Its shape is two upper loops joined by a sagging waist, with an oval below.

\subsection*{Writing: \ml{ഋ}}
One recorded hand writes \textbf{\ml{ഋ}} in two strokes. First the top: from inside the upper left loop, round it anticlockwise, down and along the waist, and up round the upper right loop, anticlockwise again. Then, after one lift, the oval below, from its top centre, clockwise.

Write \textbf{\ml{ഋ}} yourself, slowly, and larger than it is printed. Copy the printed shape and keep the order above.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Find:} \ml{ഋ} at the start of \textbf{\ml{ഋതു}}
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ml{ഋ} three times, saying \emph{ṛ} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ml{ൃ}, then \ml{ഋ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\ml{ഋതു}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ml{ഋ}? (\textbf{ṛ}, at the start of a word.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ml{ഋതു}}, \emph{ṛtu}, \textquotedblleft{}a season\textquotedblright{}.) What does it look like after a consonant? (\textbf{\ml{ൃ}}, as in \textbf{\ml{കൃഷി}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മൂന്ന്} \ml{വർഷമായി} (mūnnŭ varṣamāyi)}{മൂന്ന് വർഷമായി (mūnnŭ varṣamāyi)}]{\ml{മൂന്ന്} \ml{വർഷമായി} (mūnnŭ varṣamāyi) — for three years now}

\label{lesson:ML-C346-varsamayi}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}a year\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}an hour\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}from now on\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{varṣaṁ}, \emph{maṇikkūr}, \emph{ini mutal}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a span with -\ml{ആയി}, still running}]
To say how long something has been going on, put \textbf{-\ml{ആയി}}, \textquotedblleft{}has become\textquotedblright{}, on the span, and keep the verb in the present:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{മൂന്ന്} \ml{വർഷമായി} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{മലയാളം} \ml{പഠിക്കുന്നു}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mūnnŭ varṣamāyi ñān malayāḷaṁ paṭhikkunnu.} — \textquotedblleft{}I have been learning Malayalam for three years.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

The question puts \textbf{\ml{എത്ര}} in front: \textbf{\ml{എത്ര} \ml{വർഷമായി}?} (\emph{etra varṣamāyi?}), \textquotedblleft{}for how many years?\textquotedblright{}
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: since, and a finished span}]
\textbf{\ml{മുതൽ}}, which you know from \textbf{\ml{ഇനി} \ml{മുതൽ}}, says \textquotedblleft{}since, from\textquotedblright{}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇന്നലെ} \ml{മുതൽ} \ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{പനിയാണ്}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{innale mutal enikkŭ paniyāṇŭ.} — \textquotedblleft{}I have had a fever since yesterday.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

A span that is over takes no ending at all: the plain past says it lasted that long and stopped.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{രണ്ട്} \ml{മണിക്കൂർ} \ml{കാത്തിരുന്നു}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ñān raṇṭŭ maṇikkūr kāttirunnu.} — \textquotedblleft{}I waited for two hours.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I have been learning Malayalam for three years.\textquotedblright{}
  \item ask someone how long they have lived here — \emph{etra varṣamāyi iviṭe tāmasikkunnu?}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I have had a fever since yesterday.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I waited for two hours.\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}For three years now\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{mūnnŭ varṣamāyi}}, with the present after it.) \textquotedblleft{}Since yesterday\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{innale mutal.}}) \textquotedblleft{}I waited two hours\textquotedblright{}, over and done? (\emph{\textbf{ñān raṇṭŭ maṇikkūr kāttirunnu}}, no ending.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — comparing and time}

\label{lesson:ML-R346-comparing-and-time}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}a season\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{ṛtu}.) Write \textbf{\ml{ഋ}} once from memory, then \textbf{\ml{ഋതു}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}This is bigger than that. The train goes faster than the bus.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I like coffee more than tea.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}This is the biggest house in the village.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The rainy season is my favourite season.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I have been learning Malayalam for three years. I would like to see Kerala.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I have had a fever since yesterday. I feel tired.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}My dream is to see Kerala.\textquotedblright{} — \emph{kēraḷaṁ kāṇaṇaṁ ennāṇŭ enṟe svapnaṁ.}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}Than that\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ml{അതിനെക്കാൾ}}.) \textquotedblleft{}The most\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ml{ഏറ്റവും}}.) \textquotedblleft{}For three years now\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ml{മൂന്ന്} \ml{വർഷമായി}}.) \textquotedblleft{}Since yesterday\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ml{ഇന്നലെ} \ml{മുതൽ}}.) \textquotedblleft{}A season\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ml{ഋതു}}, which opens with \textbf{\ml{ഋ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
